sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sedet: sedeō, sedēre, sēdī — to sit (3rd sg. pres.) · also impers., it is fixed, resolved (+ dat.)
sequi: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue (pres. inf., deponent)
sequitur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, come after (3rd sg. pres. of deponent)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
seu: seu (sīve) — or if; seu… seu, whether… or
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sive: sīve (seu) — or if; sīve… sīve, whether… or
sonant: sonō, -āre, -uī, -itum — to sound, resound, rattle, speak (3rd pl. pres.)
sonat: sonō, -āre, sonuī, sonitum — to sound, resound, give forth (3rd sg. pres.)
spargit: spargō, -ere, sparsī, sparsum — to scatter, sprinkle, strew (3rd sg. pres.)
spicula: spīculum, -ī (n.) — sharp point, dart, arrowhead (acc. pl.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subibat: subeō, -īre, -iī, -itum — to go under, approach, come up to (3rd sg. impf.)
subito: subitō (adv.) — suddenly; also subitus, -a, -um, sudden (abl./dat. sg.)
sunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there are; sunt mihi, I have (3rd pl. pres.)
superbum: superbus, -a, -um — proud, haughty; splendid (m. acc. sg.)
tanto: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m./n. abl. sg.)
tegit: tegō, -ere, tēxī, tēctum — to cover, shield (3rd sg. pres.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
tendere: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, direct one's course, make for (pres. inf.)
tenuis: tenuis, -e — thin, slight, light (m./f. nom. sg.; also acc. pl. -īs)
tereti: teres, teretis — rounded, smooth, polished (f. abl. sg.)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
torquens: torqueō, -ēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, whirl, hurl, roll (pres. part., m./f. nom. sg.)
trabea: trabea, -ae (f.) — short striped robe of kings, augurs and knights (abl. sg.; also nom. sg.)
trepidus: trepidus, -a, -um — anxious, agitated, alarmed (m. nom. sg.)
trilicem: trilix, trilicis — triple-twilled, of three threads (f. acc. sg.)
tristisque: tristis, -e — sad, grim (f. acc. pl., -is for -ēs) + -que 'and' · also f. nom. sg. (tristis senectūs)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tuta: tūtus, -a, -um — safe, sheltered (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
urgueri: urgeō, -ēre, ursī — to press, weigh down (pres. pass. inf., = urguērī)
verso: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, turn round (perf. pass. part., m. abl. sg.)
vertice: vertex, verticis (m.) — peak, summit; whirl (abl. sg.)
virgulta: virgultum, -ī (n.) — brushwood, shrub, shoots (nom./acc. pl.; usually plural)
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl. (festīnāte, virī)
vocat: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd sg. pres.)
volcano: Volcānus (Vulcānus), -ī (m.) — Vulcan, god of fire; fire by metonymy (abl. sg.)
volucrum: volucris, -is (f.) — bird, winged creature (gen. pl., -um for -ium)
